premises.evidence: Array dense storage may be overridden by sidecar descriptors. Boxed String compatible virtual definitions can materialize stored numeric names/length. Virtual key construction never overlaps a different nonnumeric string.
premises.consequence: Only canonical numeric duplicates and exact virtual length need suppression. Descriptor choice remains a later live operation.

premises.evidence: json_array_index checks at most ten UTF-16 units, rejects empty/leading-zero/non-ASCII/overflow and u32::MAX. Accepted domain is canonical 0 through 4294967294. Immutable JsString Rc handles preserve exact code units.
premises.consequence: Integer index identity equals accepted numeric name identity; 01, -0, 4294967295, exponents and surrogate-containing names remain creation-ordered strings.

premises.evidence: OwnKey.rank returns only kind/index/ordinal, and monotonic scan/heapsort compare that tuple. Nonnumeric uniqueness removes the previous full-name dedup tree. Numeric duplicates are adjacent after sorting.
premises.consequence: Same classified shape has no name-length-dependent snapshot sorting/allocation; no accessor or mapped-value lookup runs during materialization.

premises.evidence: Both pinned Rust implementations use B=6, node capacity 11 and at least five non-root keys. Height h requires at least 2*6^h-1 total keys. search_tree descends one child per level; each node linearly compares each reached key at most once. BTreeSet::insert delegates to one map entry search before split propagation.
premises.consequence: min(n,11*(h+1)) is a valid upper bound on text comparisons; each comparison scans at most the incoming UTF-16 key length plus fixed overhead. Reached membership and insertion must retain separate charges.

premises.evidence: Visited starts empty and never removes. Total cumulative node allocations cannot exceed unique inserted keys; a node holds at most eleven Rc slice handles plus twelve child pointers, parent pointer and small metadata.
premises.consequence: The conservative prepaid node allowance per unique inserted key covers retained/split storage on the supported Rust layouts; it is not an exact per-call allocation report or a fallible BTreeSet reservation.
